examples.ko: 오늘은 날씨가 더없이 좋아서 점심을 공원에서 먹었어요.
examples.en: The weather was so perfect today that I ate lunch in the park.

examples.ko: 이 집은 조용해서 공부하기에 더없이 좋은 곳이에요.
examples.en: This house is quiet, so it is the best place to study.
A child's smile is the greatest joy to parents.

examples.ko: 이렇게 맛있는 음식을 먹다니 더없이 행복해요.
examples.en: I am supremely happy to eat such delicious food.
The exam is over, so my heart feels incredibly light.
I was extremely grateful that my friend helped me.

explain: '더없이 좋다, 더없이 행복하다'처럼 좋은 뜻의 말과 함께 자주 써요. '더없는 행복'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미기도 해요. '아주'보다 조금 글 같은 느낌이라 말할 때는 '정말, 너무'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is often used with positive words, as in '더없이 좋다' and '더없이 행복하다'. It can also modify a noun, as in '더없는 행복'. It feels a little more written than '아주', and in speech people also say '정말' or '너무'.

en: moral reputation; being respected for virtue

examples.en: He is famous for being highly respected in the village.
She is a teacher of fine character, so everyone respects her.
He did volunteer work for a long time to build a good name.
I asked a highly respected elder for advice.
The boss was recognized by the staff for both character and ability.

examples.ko: 덕망 높은 분이 대표가 되어서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad a person of good standing became the representative.

explain: '덕망이 높다, 덕망이 있다'처럼 써요. 인품이 훌륭해서 사람들에게 존경받는 어른이나 지도자에게 주로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '인품이 좋다, 존경받는다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used in set phrases like '덕망이 높다' and '덕망이 있다'. It mainly describes elders or leaders who are respected for their character. In everyday talk people more often say '인품이 좋다' or '존경받는다'.

examples.en: I stuck notes all over the wall.
It feels stuffy when you cake makeup on your face.

examples.ko: 낡은 문에 페인트가 덕지덕지 묻어 있어요.
examples.en: The old door is smeared thickly with paint.

examples.ko: 신발에 흙이 덕지덕지 붙어서 현관이 지저분해요.
examples.en: Mud is caked on the shoes, so the entrance is dirty.

examples.ko: 냉장고 문에 스티커가 덕지덕지 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: Stickers are plastered all over the fridge door.

examples.ko: 컵에 때가 덕지덕지 껴서 닦는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The cup was crusted with grime, so it took a long time to clean.

explain: 무언가가 많이, 두껍게 붙거나 묻어 있어서 보기에 지저분하거나 과하다는 느낌이 있어요. '붙다, 바르다, 묻다, 끼다' 같은 동사와 자주 써요. 좋은 뜻으로 쓰기보다는 조금 불만스러운 말투일 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It describes things stuck, smeared or piled on thickly, usually with a feeling that it looks messy or excessive. It goes with verbs like '붙다', '바르다', '묻다' and '끼다'. It is rarely positive and often carries a slightly displeased tone.

examples.ko: 서랍 속 그릇이 덜그럭거려서 잠을 깼어요.
examples.en: The dishes in the drawer rattled and woke me up.

examples.ko: 부엌에서 누가 접시를 덜그럭거리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: I hear someone clattering plates in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 바람이 불 때마다 낡은 창문이 덜그럭거려요.
examples.en: The old window rattles every time the wind blows.
A cart rattled through the alley.

examples.ko: 가방 안에서 동전이 덜그럭거려서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: The coins rattling in my bag bother me.
The rattling sound that went on all night stopped in the morning.

explain: 단단한 물건들이 서로 부딪혀서 나는 시끄러운 소리에 써요. '달그락거리다'도 있는데, 조금 더 작고 가벼운 소리에 쓰는 느낌이에요. '덜그럭대다'도 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: It describes the noisy sound of hard objects knocking together. '달그락거리다' also exists and feels like a smaller, lighter sound. '덜그럭대다' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: I am careless, so I often lose things.
My older sister is a scatterbrain, but she has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 덜렁이 동생이 또 우산을 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: My scatterbrained younger sibling left an umbrella behind again.

examples.ko: 덜렁이처럼 굴지 말고 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Don't be careless, and check one more time.
My friends call me a scatterbrain.

examples.ko: 덜렁이인 남편 때문에 열쇠는 항상 제가 챙겨요.
examples.en: Because my husband is forgetful, I always keep the keys.

explain: 침착하지 못하고 자주 실수하거나 물건을 잘 잃어버리는 사람을 가볍게 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 친한 사이나 자기 자신에게 쓰면 괜찮지만, 처음 만난 사람이나 어른에게는 조심하는 게 좋아요. '덜렁대다'처럼 동사로도 말해요.
explain_en: It teases someone who is hasty, makes mistakes often or loses things. It is fine with close friends or about yourself, but be careful with strangers or elders. The verb form '덜렁대다' is also used.

en: nape; the back of the neck

examples.en: A cold wind is blowing and the back of my neck feels chilly.
The thief was caught by the police.
The police grabbed the fleeing person by the scruff of the neck.
I was sweating, so I wiped the back of my neck with a towel.

examples.ko: 누가 목덜미를 만지는 것 같아서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because it felt like someone touched the back of my neck.

examples.ko: 거짓말을 많이 해서 언젠가 덜미를 잡힐까 불안해요.
examples.en: I've told so many lies that I'm anxious I'll get caught someday.

explain: 몸을 말할 때는 '목덜미'라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많고, '덜미'만 쓰는 건 주로 '덜미를 잡다/잡히다'일 때예요. '덜미를 잡히다'는 나쁜 일이 들켜서 붙잡힌다는 느낌이라 뉴스나 드라마에서도 나와요.

phrases.example: 숨기던 일이 들통나서 결국 덜미를 잡혔어요.
phrases.en: The thing I was hiding came out, and I finally got caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이나 비밀이 드러나서 꼼짝 못 하게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a bad deed or secret is exposed and you are cornered.

explain_en: For the body part, people usually say '목덜미', and '덜미' alone appears mostly in '덜미를 잡다/잡히다'. '덜미를 잡히다' has the feeling of being caught for something bad, and it shows up in news and dramas too.

examples.en: He took the bad news calmly.
My friend told me her story in a matter-of-fact way.
Even after we broke up, we greeted each other without much feeling.
My father said "It's fine" in a calm, plain voice.

examples.ko: 합격 소식을 듣고도 덤덤히 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: Even after hearing I had passed, I just sat there calmly.
It was a sad matter, but she smiled quietly.

explain: 기쁘거나 슬픈 일이 있어도 감정을 크게 드러내지 않고 조용히 대하는 모습이에요. '말하다, 받아들이다, 대하다' 같은 동사와 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '담담히'가 있어요.
explain_en: It describes dealing with something quietly without showing strong emotion, whether it is happy or sad. It is often used with verbs like '말하다', '받아들이다' and '대하다'. A similar word is '담담히'.

examples.ko: 동료의 실수 때문에 제가 덤터기를 썼어요.
examples.en: I got stuck with the blame because of my coworker's mistake.
Why are you trying to pin it on me?

examples.ko: 남의 잘못으로 덤터기를 쓰는 건 정말 억울해요.
examples.en: It is really unfair to take the blame for someone else's fault.
He took all the blame for the accident alone.

examples.ko: 아무 잘못도 없는데 덤터기를 쓸까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I did nothing wrong, but I worry I'll be blamed.

examples.ko: 친구가 일을 망쳐 놓고 저한테 덤터기를 씌웠어요.
examples.en: My friend ruined the work and then pinned the blame on me.

explain: 거의 '덤터기를 쓰다'와 '덤터기를 씌우다' 두 가지 모양으로 써요. '쓰다'는 내가 억울하게 떠안는 것이고, '씌우다'는 남에게 떠넘기는 거예요. 비슷하게 '뒤집어쓰다, 뒤집어씌우다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '덤터기를 쓰다' or '덤터기를 씌우다'. '쓰다' means you take on the blame unfairly, and '씌우다' means you push it onto someone else. People also say '뒤집어쓰다' and '뒤집어씌우다' in a similar way.

examples.en: The child suddenly grabbed my hand.
The puppy snapped up the treat.
It is risky to sign a contract right away just because the terms look good.
He readily accepted my request.
My friend was so happy to see me that she hugged me.

examples.ko: 낯선 사람이 주는 걸 덥석 받지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't just take something a stranger offers you.

explain: 망설이지 않고 갑자기 잡거나 물거나 받아들이는 모습이에요. 손을 잡을 때뿐 아니라 제안이나 선물을 생각 없이 받을 때도 써요. 껴안을 때는 '와락'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.example: 좋은 조건이라는 말에 미끼를 덥석 물었다가 후회했어요.
phrases.en: I took the bait right away because the terms sounded good, and I regretted it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달콤한 말이나 유혹에 깊이 생각하지 않고 넘어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone falls for tempting words or an offer without thinking.

explain_en: It describes grabbing, biting or accepting something suddenly and without hesitation. It is used not only for grabbing a hand but also for taking an offer or gift without thinking. For hugging, '와락' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: My hair is shaggy, so I need to go to the hair salon.
He showed up with a bushy beard.
My older brother, whom I hadn't seen in a while, had shaggy hair.
I want to tidy up my shaggy bangs.
My eyebrows grew bushy, so I trimmed them.
The puppy's fur is too shaggy.

explain: 머리카락, 수염, 털이 길고 많이 나서 정리가 안 된 모습에 써요. 단정하지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 '머리가 덥수룩해요'는 이발할 때가 됐다는 말로도 들려요. '텁수룩하다'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes hair, beard or fur that is long, thick and untidy. It carries a feeling of looking unkempt, so '머리가 덥수룩해요' hints that a haircut is due. '텁수룩하다' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: The wind was strong, so I closed the outer shutters.

examples.ko: 시골집 창문 밖에는 나무 덧문이 있어요.
examples.en: The country house has wooden outer shutters outside the windows.

examples.ko: 시골 가게 덧문이 이미 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The country store's outer shutters were already closed.
In winter we put up an extra door to block the cold wind.

examples.ko: 덧문을 열자 아침 햇살이 방 안으로 들어왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the shutters, the morning sunlight came into the room.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 덧문은 열 때마다 삐걱거려요.
examples.en: The outer door at Grandma's house creaks every time it is opened.

explain: 문이나 창문 바깥쪽에 하나 더 덧대어 다는 문이에요. 요즘 가게의 내려오는 문은 '셔터'라고 많이 말하고, '덧문'은 시골집이나 옛날 집 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is an extra door or shutter fixed on the outside of a door or window. For a shop's pull-down door, people often say '셔터' these days, while '덧문' appears more in talk about country or old houses.

examples.ko: 파운데이션을 덧발랐더니 얼굴이 너무 하얘 보여요.
examples.en: I put on more foundation and now my face looks too white.

examples.ko: 벽에 페인트를 한 번 더 덧발랐어요.
examples.en: I put another coat of paint on the wall.

examples.ko: 선크림은 두 시간마다 덧바르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to reapply sunscreen every two hours.
When I reapply lip balm, my lips feel moist.

examples.ko: 약을 덧바르지 말고 얇게 한 번만 바르세요.
examples.en: Don't layer on the ointment; apply it thinly just once.

examples.ko: 얼룩이 보여서 그 위에 덧발라 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a stain, so I tried covering it with another layer.

explain: '르' 불규칙이라 '덧발라요, 덧발랐어요'가 돼요. 이미 바른 곳에 한 번 더 바를 때 쓰고, 페인트처럼 색을 입히는 경우에는 '덧칠하다'도 많이 말해요. 말을 더 보탤 때는 '덧붙이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '덧발라요' and '덧발랐어요'. It is used for applying another layer on a spot already covered, and for paint or color '덧칠하다' is also common. To add more words to what you said, use '덧붙이다'.

examples.en: In winter, wearing extra socks keeps my feet warm.

examples.ko: 신발 안에 보이지 않는 덧신을 신었어요.
examples.en: I wore no-show socks inside my shoes.
The footies keep slipping off, which is annoying.
I bought footies and sneakers together.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 신발 위에 덧신을 신었어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day I put overshoes on top of my shoes.

examples.ko: 선물로 귀여운 덧신을 한 켤레 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a pair of cute footies as a gift.

explain: 신발이나 양말 위에 덧신는 것을 말하고, 발목이 안 보이게 짧은 양말을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요. 한 켤레, 두 켤레로 세고 '신다, 벗다'와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It means something worn over shoes or socks, and it is also commonly used for very short socks that don't show at the ankle. Count them with '켤레' and use verbs like '신다' and '벗다'.
